title: 1973 AHSME Problem 32
statement: The volume of a pyramid whose base is an equilateral triangle of side length \(6\) and whose other edges are each of length \(\sqrt{15}\) is

solutions.text:
The base area is \[ \frac{\sqrt3}{4}(6^2)=9\sqrt3. \] Because the apex is equally distant from all three base vertices, its perpendicular projection is the base circumcenter. The circumradius of the equilateral base is \(\frac{6}{\sqrt3}=2\sqrt3.\) If \(h\) is the pyramid’s height, then \[ h^2+(2\sqrt3)^2=(\sqrt{15})^2, \] so \(h=\sqrt3.\) The volume is \[ \frac13(9\sqrt3)(\sqrt3)=9. \]

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: The altitude from the apex meets the base at the equilateral triangle’s circumcenter
Use the base circumradius \(2\sqrt3\) and a lateral edge \(\sqrt{15}\) to find the height
